Description

Phospholipase C enzymes cleave PI(4,5)P2 into DAG and IP3 in nociceptors. PLCβ is driven by Gq-coupled receptors such as the bradykinin B2 receptor, and PLCγ1 by NGF through its tyrosine kinase receptor TrkA. IP3 releases Ca2+ from the endoplasmic reticulum, which opens ANO1 chloride channels, depolarises the neuron and triggers action potentials. Antibodies against NGF such as tanezumab reduce knee OA pain.

Colour

Proteins and metabolites are coloured by their contribution to pain: red for those that raise it (they excite or sensitise nociceptive neurons, or drive the inflammation that does), blue for those that relieve it, and olive for the shared signalling machinery (G proteins, RGS, adenylate cyclase, phospholipases, kinases, adaptors, second messengers, ions and nucleotides), whose effect is set by the receptor upstream. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white. Each molecule is coloured by its role in this block, so the same molecule can be red in one block and blue in another.

NGF and its receptor TrkA are red. An antibody against NGF, tanezumab, reduced joint pain in patients with OA but was followed by rapidly progressive OA in some of them (Schnitzer 2019): relief of pain and the fate of the joint can part, which these colours do not show.
